title: RizzitGO shipping calculator: estimate a parcel before you buy
summary: Build a freight estimate from the destination, item category, packed weight and dimensions, then compare two routes on equal terms.

sections.heading: Start with a decision you can actually make
paragraphs: A pair of shoes costs less than your budget, but you still need to get it from the warehouse to your door. Entering a convenient round number into a freight calculator produces a price quickly. The harder question is whether the price answers anything. Are you deciding whether to buy the shoes, whether to keep the retail box, or whether two items should travel together? Write down that decision before looking at a route. It tells you which unknown could change your answer.

On the product page, record the item price and selected size. Start a separate line for international shipping. The currency selector helps you read the item price, while the RizzitGO freight calculator uses parcel information. A product price that looks affordable in your home currency tells you very little about the dimensions of the box that will arrive.

sections.heading: Enter the destination and describe the contents
paragraphs: Open the official freight calculator and choose the country or region where someone will receive the package. Enter the province or state when relevant. Pick the category that describes what you plan to ship. In the weight field, check the unit beside the input. One and a half kilograms should be entered as 1,500 grams if the field asks for grams. That single conversion is worth checking before drawing a conclusion from an unexpectedly low quote.

Enter the outer length, width and height in centimetres when you have them. A seller's shoe length or a jacket's chest measurement belongs to the product and cannot stand in for the carton. Before purchase, mark any guessed number as an assumption. After warehouse packing, replace it with the measured number. Keep those two versions so you can explain a change in cost.

sections.heading: Test the carton as well as the scale weight
paragraphs: Suppose the planned package weighs 1,800 grams. Compare two hypothetical cartons measuring 34 by 24 by 15 centimetres and 40 by 30 by 20 centimetres. Their volumes are 12,240 and 24,000 cubic centimetres. The second occupies nearly twice the space despite having the same scale weight in this example. If the route takes parcel volume into account, two estimates using 1,800 grams alone may hide the very difference you need to understand.

Run the two cases through the same calculator for the same destination and item category. Keep the dimensions beside the results. An example divisor in a third-party weight tool can illustrate the calculation, but only use it for an actual decision when the selected route gives that rule. Look at the billing mode, chargeable weight and displayed price on the route itself. A dimensional estimate is useful even when its main result is a question to send to the warehouse.

sections.heading: Read an available route from left to right
paragraphs: First check that the calculator lists the route as available for the details entered. Next record the displayed freight amount and currency, the transit estimate, the billing basis and any service or coverage terms that matter to you. Two route names containing the same carrier name can describe different products. Save the complete route label. If the page displays a promotion, check whether it applies to your account and that specific route before including it in your budget.

Imagine one option fits your budget only with a coupon, while another fits without one. The decision turns on the first route's eligibility conditions. Open its details and check the checkout figure. If you cannot establish eligibility before buying the goods, use the undiscounted case for planning. This leaves room for the purchase decision to make sense even if the discount disappears.

sections.heading: Work through an empty route list
paragraphs: An empty result is still useful. Recheck the destination, gram units, category and each dimension against your notes. A misplaced decimal can turn an ordinary parcel into apparently oversized freight. If your inputs are correct, check the logistics notices and read any reason attached to an unavailable line. A route can exclude a category or simply be unavailable for the chosen destination and measurements.

When asking support, send the destination region, accurate description of the goods, total weight, dimensions and full route name if one appeared. A screenshot showing the fields alongside the result is more useful than a cropped price. If you want to compare a second packing plan, describe what will actually change. Calling an electronic item clothing to make a quote appear will give you an estimate for a different shipment.

sections.heading: Decide what the quote leaves out
paragraphs: Put the purchase price, seller delivery within China, international freight and any services you select on separate lines. Use the amounts shown for your order. Leave unknown amounts open; typing zero makes them easy to overlook later. Under your total, write down any specific assumptions about retail packaging, the exchange rate or a discount. Reopen the estimate if one of those assumptions changes before shipment.

For a shared parcel, agree how to divide freight before anyone pays. Splitting a measured charge equally is easy to explain when similar items occupy similar space. It can produce a surprising result when one person's retail box dictates the outer carton. Compare the estimate with and without that box and discuss the difference. The calculator gives the group evidence for a conversation; it cannot choose the arrangement for you.

sections.heading: Reconcile the estimate at parcel submission
paragraphs: When the warehouse measurements become available, enter them again and reopen the eligible route. Compare the new chargeable weight with the one you saved. Then compare the service choices and final amount on the parcel screen. A difference can come from a larger carton, an added service or a different route. Checking one field at a time is more informative than comparing two isolated totals.

Keep the original estimate, the confirmed parcel details and the final charge together. If an amount remains unexplained, ask about the particular line before proceeding. For example, “Which outer dimensions were used for this route?” is a more answerable question than “Why is shipping expensive?” The resulting record also gives you a better starting point the next time you estimate a similar purchase.

title: RizzitGO parcel consolidation: when to combine warehouse items
summary: Compare one parcel with a split shipment, protect the items that need it, and give the warehouse packing instructions it can act on.

sections.heading: Begin with the warehouse inventory
paragraphs: Consolidation starts with a list of what has actually reached the warehouse. A sweatshirt in storage, shoes awaiting inspection and a cap the seller has yet to dispatch are three different decisions. RizzitGO describes selecting stored items in the Warehouse area before proceeding to parcel checkout. Open each relevant record and note its item identifier, selected option, quantity and current stage. Keep anything still under review out of the first packing plan.

Add one more column that only you can fill in: what must arrive in good condition? For a sweatshirt it might be the garment alone. For a collectible, the retail packaging could be part of the purchase. For a gift, the date may matter more than either box size or a small freight saving. These answers determine which combinations are worth pricing. Simply adding up every item in your account does not resolve those competing needs.

sections.heading: Design two plausible parcels
paragraphs: Consider an illustrative order containing sneakers in a presentation box, two folded cotton shirts and a structured cap. The shirts can be folded. The cap needs room above its crown. The sneakers may travel with or without their presentation box depending on your preference. First sketch a single parcel that preserves the cap's shape and the shoe box. Then sketch a second plan in which the cap travels separately. Ask which outer dimensions the warehouse expects for each plan if the decision depends on them.

Compare both arrangements for the same destination and item descriptions in the freight calculator. For the split plan, add both freight figures and any packing services required for each parcel. A lower number on one of the two smaller parcels can look attractive until you include its companion. Conversely, a single larger carton may change the available route. Avoid promising friends that consolidation will save money before calculating both complete alternatives.

sections.heading: Identify packaging that carries information
paragraphs: Before requesting box or tag removal, inspect the listing and warehouse pictures. You may need a size sticker to distinguish two similar pairs, a label to match a purchase record or a box to present a gift. If two nearly identical items will go to different recipients, write down how you will identify each after unboxing. Ask for the relevant photo while the item and the information are still together.

Suppose both shirts are black and differ only by size. Keeping a visible size label with each is more useful than saving an image of two folded shirts side by side. If you want the shoe box discarded but the labels on the shirts retained, specify that distinction. One instruction applied indiscriminately to the whole parcel can solve the wrong problem. Confirm any associated service price before selecting it.

sections.heading: Describe the packing result in plain language
paragraphs: The official buying guide lists optional parcel services including packaging removal and reinforcement. Write one short instruction per item, tied to the warehouse identifier. An example for the mixed parcel would be “Keep the original sneaker box for item A. Keep the cap upright for item B. Fold the two shirts separately with their size labels visible.” Replace the example letters with the actual identifiers before you send anything.

“Pack carefully” offers little guidance when priorities conflict. Tell the warehouse whether you value a smaller outer carton, an intact retail box or extra space around a shaped object. If keeping a box intact is essential, ask what protection is possible and what it adds to the dimensions. Reinforcing the outside and supporting a cap from the inside address different problems. Ask for confirmation when the available service name does not tell you which one you are buying.

sections.heading: Compare departure dates alongside money
paragraphs: One late item can hold up several ready ones. Write the date you would choose to ship the ready pieces and the latest date on which waiting for the missing item still serves your plans. Check any storage deadline displayed for each item in your own account. Two pieces received on different days need their own checks. Review the actual extension options if you expect to wait, especially before making a shipment decision for someone else.

For example, a gift intended for an upcoming trip and casual clothing with no deadline need not share a departure date. Price the gift separately and compare the extra expense with the cost of missing the occasion. A transit estimate describes a route after dispatch under its stated conditions. Waiting for a seller to send an item and waiting for the warehouse to assemble a parcel belong on your own timeline.

sections.heading: Choose eligible routes for the entire contents
paragraphs: Check that every item fits the terms of the selected line. A route suitable for the shirts alone may give a different answer once another type of item is included. If eligibility is uncertain, describe the item accurately and ask the platform about the combination. Recheck the actual country, region, telephone number and delivery address on each parcel. A split shipment gives you two opportunities for an address detail to go wrong.

Write the two candidate plans on separate lines with the parcel contents, outer dimensions, measured or estimated weight, route, packing choices and total. Circle any figure still based on a guess. This makes the point of disagreement visible: perhaps you are comfortable with the freight amount but do not know whether a shoe box can survive the chosen arrangement. Resolve that question before committing the contents.

sections.heading: Keep a parcel-level record
paragraphs: After confirming the plan, save the final item list alongside its parcel identifier. For a split shipment, label the two records by contents instead of calling them simply “first” and “second.” The one that leaves first may arrive last. When a delivery notification appears, you will know precisely which items you should find in that box and which belong to a parcel still in transit.

Check the exterior on receipt and compare the contents with the saved list as you unpack. If something appears absent, consult the second parcel record before reporting a shortage. If there is real damage, keep the packaging and document the affected item and its identifier for the official after-sales channel. A few minutes spent mapping items to parcels before dispatch can spare a much longer investigation afterward.

title: RizzitGO tracking: find the right number and read the latest scan
summary: Distinguish a seller delivery from an international parcel, interpret tracking events and prepare a useful support enquiry.

sections.heading: Find the number attached to the shipment
paragraphs: A buyer opens a marketplace tracking page and sees “delivered.” Nothing has reached their home. The first question is which journey the number describes. A seller may send an item to the warehouse before the warehouse packs an international parcel. If the order is still listed as stored, a completed delivery on the seller's record can be entirely consistent with the international journey having yet to begin. Look at the destination and order stage before raising a delivery complaint.

RizzitGO's official buying guide directs customers to the tracking option in Package Details. Open the parcel that contains the item you are waiting for. Copy the shipment number from that record and write down the route name and parcel identifier beside it. The number printed in a product link identifies merchandise. The parcel identifier helps customer service find your warehouse record. The carrier's tracking number is the one to enter in the tracking tool.

sections.heading: Start an event log you can read later
paragraphs: The official RizzitGO Track site lets you add a tracking number and groups parcels by status. Start there or follow the tracking link in your own parcel record. Keep the original event text with its timestamp and location, especially when the English translation seems vague. If a carrier is named, consult that carrier's page for the same number. When the parcel record provides a separate local delivery number, label it as such in your notes.

A simple example entry is “Tuesday, 18:40, dispatch information received, origin facility, international number ending 4821.” Use invented digits only in practice notes and keep real tracking details private. Add a later entry underneath instead of overwriting the first. This preserves the difference between a message appearing on your screen today and an event that took place yesterday. If timestamps use different time zones, preserve the labels before trying to put the events in order.

sections.heading: Read a label event literally
paragraphs: A newly issued label can appear before the first physical carrier scan. UPS, for example, explains that its label-created status records receipt of shipment information; the carrier updates the status when it has the package and it starts moving. Other carriers use their own wording. Read their definition when possible and look for a handover, acceptance or facility event before concluding that transport has started.

An empty result needs a different check. Compare every character with the number in Package Details, remove spaces inserted by copying and verify that you chose the right parcel. If the number belongs to a domestic seller shipment, go back to the international parcel record. If the platform has not provided an international number yet, ask about dispatch under the parcel identifier. Repeating a product ID in several tracking sites cannot reveal a shipment bearing another number.

sections.heading: Decide what a quiet interval means
paragraphs: Tracking is a succession of recorded events. You might see a departure and then a long gap before the next facility records an arrival. A quiet interval alone does not identify where a parcel is or what has happened to it. Compare the last event with the route information saved at submission. Check whether the displayed time range refers to transit or includes other steps. Use any service-specific guidance from the platform or carrier to decide when an enquiry is appropriate.

Suppose a Saturday screenshot shows the same Wednesday departure as a screenshot taken on Friday. The new screenshot is useful evidence that the display has not changed; it does not constitute another departure or prove the parcel spent three days at the named location. If the estimate has passed, ask which organisation has the most recent physical scan and whether a local number is available. This gives support a specific gap to investigate.

sections.heading: Handle delivery and exception messages differently
paragraphs: An exception describes an issue worth reading, rather than a single universal outcome. It could be accompanied by a new delivery estimate or a request for information. Read the full event and check the official carrier page for actions addressed to the recipient. If it asks for address clarification, open the carrier's or platform's website yourself and use the contact method there. A tracking screenshot shared on a forum is a poor place to post an address, contact number or identity document.

A delivered scan calls for a physical check. Read the location, time and any available proof of delivery. Check an agreed reception desk, parcel locker or pickup point where appropriate. A collection-point delivery and a handover to someone at your home are different outcomes. If the recorded location does not match the instructions, contact the named delivery operator and the platform through their official channels. Keep the event screenshot and any case reference.

sections.heading: Send an enquiry someone can act on
paragraphs: Include the parcel identifier, route name, tracking number, last meaningful event and date in your private support message. Describe the single decision you need help with. For a quiet shipment, ask whether the carrier accepted it and whether a local tracking number exists. For an apparent misdelivery, ask for the delivery location or available proof. Avoid attaching unrelated screenshots from all your other orders; they can lead the recipient to investigate the wrong package.

For example, a useful message says that parcel A contains the cap and shirts, that the latest carrier event was a facility arrival on Monday, and that the reference shown in Package Details still matches. Add that the expected delivery window shown for this parcel has passed, if that is true. Ask which party will open the trace and where the response will appear. Save the answer and its date so a follow-up can begin with that case.

sections.heading: Close the record at the right moment
paragraphs: When the package arrives, match it to the parcel list and check the contents before confirming receipt in your account. For a split shipment, close the record for the box actually received and leave the other one open. If condition or contents need attention, photograph the outer packaging, shipping label and affected item, then use the parcel's after-sales option. Keep personal details out of any public review. The useful end of the tracking record is the point where you know which box arrived, what it contained and whether anything remains for support to resolve.
